spec_family.name: Exterior Caulking (New Construction)
spec_family.description: Standalone LF-based exterior caulking for paintable joints on new construction. Covers sealant application across all exterior joint locations — trim-to-siding, window perimeter, corner board, penetration, and expansion joints. Four paintable sealant types (acrylic_latex, siliconized_acrylic, polyurethane, hybrid_ms) as primary configuration dimension replacing quality tier. Two joint complexity tiers (simple_bead, backer_rod) drive production rate bifurcation. Silicone is excluded — never paintable. Caulking must occur AFTER substrate primer and BEFORE finish coats, creating inter-spec sequencing dependencies with all exterior painting specs. No quality tier, no substrate_state, no access modifier (shared with adjacent painting spec).

includes: Joint preparation — dust/debris removal from new construction joint cavities
Backer rod installation for joints > 3/8 inch wide (closed-cell foam, sized 1.25x joint width)
Sealant application — gun and tool to concave profile with two-sided adhesion
Four paintable sealant types: acrylic_latex, siliconized_acrylic, polyurethane, hybrid_ms
Five joint location categories: trim_to_siding, window_perimeter, corner_board, penetration, expansion
Ground protection (drop cloth for sealant drips)
Adjacent surface tape masking (conditional — finished surfaces only)
Joint inspection — visual continuity check and spot adhesion verification
Material staging — sealant tubes, caulk gun, backer rod, utility knife
Cleanup — tape removal, drop cloth removal, waste disposal, tool cleaning

excludes.route_to: Non-paint scope — silicone is never paintable. Applied AFTER all painting is complete on non-paintable joints only.

excludes.item: Structural adhesive joints, fire-stop sealants, below-grade waterproofing
excludes.route_to: Specialty contractor — different trade, different materials, different standards
Adjacent painting spec — caulking shares access setup with painting spec covering same elevation per KD-012. Double-counting prevention.
Future SF_CAULK_EXT_RP_v1 — NC joints are open and clean, no existing sealant to remove

excludes.item: Paint/primer application over cured caulk joints
excludes.route_to: Adjacent painting specs (SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1, SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT_v1, SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC_v1, etc.) — finish coats applied by the surface spec, not the caulk spec

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary sealant type for paintable joints. Drives material cost, cure time (scheduling impact), movement capacity, and lifespan. Replaces quality_tier as the cost/quality driver for this spec.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Silicone excluded — never paintable. Acrylic_latex = lowest cost, immediate paint, 5-10 yr. Siliconized_acrylic = mid-range, immediate paint, 10-15 yr. Polyurethane = high movement Class 25/50, 3-7 day cure gate, 15-25 yr. Hybrid_ms = premium, 1-2 hr paint wait, 20-30 yr.

configuration_dimensions.description: Joint complexity tier driving production rate bifurcation and backer rod material activation. Determined by joint width — joints > 3/8 inch auto-escalate to backer_rod.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Simple_bead = gun-and-tool, 100-150 LF/hr. Backer_rod = backer rod install + sealant + tool, 75-100 LF/hr. Backer rod prevents three-sided adhesion and controls sealant depth (2:1 width:depth ratio). Both tiers may coexist on the same project.

paintable_items.name: Exterior Caulk Joint
paintable_items.counting_rules: Measured in linear feet of joint. Sum of all exterior caulk joints across all joint locations (trim-to-siding, window perimeter, corner board, penetration, expansion). Each joint measured as continuous run. Not a painted surface — the sealant bead IS the deliverable. Downstream painting specs apply finish coats over cured sealant.
paintable_items.notes: Nominal 'paintable' designation — the item represents the caulked joint which is subsequently painted by adjacent surface specs. No single PS_EXT key exists for caulk LF; estimator captures joint quantities directly during takeoff.

variants.notes: BASELINE ECONOMY. Acrylic latex on simple joints. Lowest cost, immediate paint, 5-10 yr lifespan. Best for low-movement trim-to-siding and window perimeter joints.
Acrylic latex on wide joints (> 3/8 inch). Backer rod install + sealant. Acrylic has low movement capacity — verify joint is truly low-movement before using on wide joints.
Siliconized acrylic on simple joints. Mid-range cost, improved water resistance, immediate paint, 10-15 yr lifespan.
Siliconized acrylic on wide joints. Still low-movement class — same constraint as acrylic on wide joints.

PREMIUM MOVEMENT. Polyurethane on simple joints. Class 25/50 movement. SCHEDULING IMPACT: 3-7 day cure gate before finish coats. 15-25 yr lifespan. Best for expansion joints and high-movement applications.
Polyurethane on wide joints with backer rod. Typical for expansion joints — widest joints with highest movement. 3-7 day cure gate applies.

PREMIUM. Hybrid MS polymer on simple joints. Combines silicone-like durability with paintability. Class 25 movement. 1-2 hr paint wait (no multi-day cure gate). 20-30 yr lifespan. Highest cost among paintable sealants.
Hybrid MS polymer on wide joints with backer rod. Premium option for wide joints needing medium movement capacity without polyurethane cure delay.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Total linear feet of all exterior caulk joints in scope. Direct estimator capture during takeoff. Sum of all joint locations (trim-to-siding, window perimeter, corner board, penetration, expansion).

required_paintscope_inputs.required_when: Joint width > 3/8 inch on any subset of total joint LF
required_paintscope_inputs.description: Subset of total joint LF requiring backer rod installation (joints > 3/8 inch wide). Drives joint_complexity split. Simple bead LF = total - backer_rod.
Primary sealant type for paintable joints. One of: acrylic_latex, siliconized_acrylic, polyurethane, hybrid_ms. Drives material system selection and scheduling gate (polyurethane).

protection_zones_required.notes: Drop cloth directly below caulking work area. Minimal coverage — caulking produces very little debris. Catches sealant drips and cut-off bead waste. Lightweight canvas or plastic acceptable.

Painter's tape along both sides of joint on finished/visible surfaces for clean sealant lines. Not all joints require taping — conditional on finished adjacent surfaces. Tape removed before sealant skins (time-sensitive).

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Siding field surface adjacent to trim-to-siding caulk joints. Caulk joint runs along the boundary between siding and trim. Protection-only relationship — siding is painted by its own spec.
Vertical corner board joints. Caulk runs both edges of corner boards (2x corner LF).
Window perimeter caulk joints. Caulk runs along casing-to-wall joint around window openings.
Door perimeter caulk joints. Caulk runs along casing-to-wall joint around door openings.

valid_input_states.notes: New construction scope — joints are open, clean, and unfinished. NC joints have no existing sealant. Single input state for all NC caulking.

output_state.notes: Output state is a caulked joint ready for paint overcoat by adjacent painting spec. Sealant bead is the deliverable — not a painted surface. Downstream painting specs apply finish coats over the cured sealant to create a continuous weatherproof envelope.

site_condition_rules.effect: simple_bead activates TSK_CAULK_APPLY_SIMPLE (125 LF/hr), excludes TSK_CAULK_BACKER_ROD and TSK_CAULK_APPLY_BACKER. backer_rod activates TSK_CAULK_BACKER_ROD (175 LF/hr) and TSK_CAULK_APPLY_BACKER (87 LF/hr), excludes TSK_CAULK_APPLY_SIMPLE.
site_condition_rules.notes: Task selection factor — not a rate multiplier. Each task variant has its own calibrated base rate. Auto-escalate to backer_rod when joint width > 3/8 inch.

site_condition_rules.affected_tasks: All apply tasks (material selection), all downstream painting tasks (scheduling gate for polyurethane)
site_condition_rules.effect: acrylic_latex=SYS_EXT_CAULK_ACRYLIC (paint immediately). siliconized_acrylic=SYS_EXT_CAULK_SILICONIZED (paint immediately). polyurethane=SYS_EXT_CAULK_POLYURETHANE (3-7 day cure gate). hybrid_ms=SYS_EXT_CAULK_HYBRID (paint after 1-2 hr skin).
site_condition_rules.notes: Primary driver for material cost and scheduling impact. Polyurethane introduces GATE_CAULK_POLY_CURE blocking all finish coats on adjacent painting specs.

hard_stops.description: Silicone sealant must NEVER be used on joints that will be painted. Silicone repels all paint — paint will not adhere to silicone or silicone residue. If silicone was previously applied to a joint that now needs painting, the silicone must be completely removed. No solvent or primer can create adhesion over silicone.
hard_stops.notes: Absolute prohibition. Engine must reject silicone as a sealant_type option.

hard_stops.action: GATE — enforce 3-7 day cure before painting
hard_stops.description: When sealant_type = polyurethane, a mandatory 3-7 day full cure gate must be enforced before ANY paint or primer is applied over caulked joints. Water from paint causes flash cure and surface bubbling. Caulk beads (~40 mils) shrink as they cure — paint film (1-3 mils) cracks if applied too early.
hard_stops.notes: Scheduling gate — not a hard stop on caulking work itself. Blocks downstream painting. No exceptions regardless of weather, urgency, or tier.

hard_stops.description: Joints wider than 3/8 inch must use backer rod. Without backer rod, wide joints have improper width:depth ratio and risk three-sided adhesion (sealant bonded to sidewalls AND joint bottom), causing premature cohesive failure. Backer rod diameter = joint width x 1.25 for compression fit.
hard_stops.notes: Auto-escalation rule — system must override simple_bead to backer_rod when joint width > 3/8 inch. Not a work-stop, but a mandatory complexity upgrade.

scheduling_gates.blocks: All finish coat tasks in adjacent painting specs (SF_TRIM_EXT_NC_v1, SF_WOOD_SIDING_EXT_NC_PAINT_v1, SF_SIDING_FIBERCEMENT_EXT_NC_v1, SF_WINDOW_EXT_NC_v1, SF_DOOR_EXT_NC_v1)
scheduling_gates.description: Polyurethane sealant requires 3-7 day full cure before any paint or primer can be applied over caulked joints. No exceptions.
scheduling_gates.resolution: Schedule caulking early in project. Use acrylic, siliconized, or hybrid_ms if polyurethane cure time is unacceptable for the schedule.

scheduling_gates.prerequisite: Substrate primer on adjacent surfaces must be applied BEFORE caulking begins
scheduling_gates.description: Caulk adheres better to primed surfaces. Priming first seals the substrate and prevents sealant adhesion failure from substrate outgassing. Sequence: substrate primer -> caulk -> cure -> finish coats.

xspec_flags_set.description: Set when all caulk joints are applied and skinned/cured. Adjacent painting specs should check this flag before applying finish coats over caulked joints.
Set when sealant_type = polyurethane. Signals 3-7 day cure delay before finish coats. Blocks painting spec finish phases.

cross_spec_coordination.deduplication_note: Caulking is a standalone line item — NOT embedded in any adjacent painting spec. All joint locations are captured here. No overlap with painting spec scope.
cross_spec_coordination.shared_session_note: Caulking is performed during the same access/staging setup as painting. No separate mobilization. Caulking crew works during the same site visit as the painting crew.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Protect (ground cover, tape masking if finished surfaces) → Stage Materials (sealant, gun, backer rod) → Joint Prep (clean all joints) → Backer Rod Install (wide joints only) → Apply Sealant (simple_bead joints first, then backer_rod joints) → Inspect (visual + spot adhesion) → Tape Remove (time-sensitive — before sealant skins) → Cleanup (drop cloth, waste disposal, tool cleaning)
sequencing_notes.inter_spec_sequence: Adjacent painting spec substrate primer → THIS SPEC caulk application → Cure period (polyurethane: 3-7 days, hybrid: 1-2 hr, acrylic/siliconized: 30 min) → Adjacent painting spec finish coats
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO silicone on paintable joints. NO painting over uncured polyurethane. NO wide joints (> 3/8 inch) without backer rod. NO three-sided adhesion (backer rod or bond-breaker tape mandatory). NO caulking wet/frost-covered joints. NO leaving tape overnight (remove before sealant skins).

movement_class_routing.description: Sealant type selection guidance based on expected joint movement. Decision support for estimators — not an engine rule.

relationships.cross_spec_protection_note: Caulking shares access equipment with adjacent painting spec — no separate access mobilization. Ground protection is caulking-specific (lightweight edge-only). Adjacent surface tape masking is caulking-specific (clean sealant lines). No overlap with painting spec protection zones.
relationships.notes: First exterior caulking spec. Establishes LF-based joint estimation pattern, sealant_type configuration dimension (replacing quality_tier), joint_complexity task selection, and inter-spec sequencing gates (XSPEC_CAULK_COMPLETE, XSPEC_CAULK_POLY_CURE_GATE). Patterns established here inform future SF_CAULK_EXT_RP_v1 (repaint caulking with old caulk removal).

research_corrections.corrected_to: 4 paintable sealant types: acrylic_latex, siliconized_acrylic, polyurethane, hybrid_ms
research_corrections.rationale: Doctrine defines siliconized acrylic as a distinct paintable sealant type with improved water resistance and 10-15 year lifespan. It fills the gap between acrylic_latex and polyurethane in the sealant performance spectrum.

research_corrections.corrected_to: No separate height/access modifier — shared cost assumption with painting spec
research_corrections.rationale: Caulking is performed during the same access setup as painting. Adding a separate access modifier would double-count access costs. Production rates assume access already in place.

sections_used: Sequencing — caulk after primer, before finish coats (§3)
Failure modes — adhesive and cohesive failure (§4)
Shared access cost assumption (no separate access modifier for caulking)

change_log.author: SpecFactory Assembly Agent
change_log.changes: Initial draft spec for exterior caulking (new construction). FIRST EXTERIOR CAULKING SPEC — introduces standalone LF-based caulk joint estimation, sealant_type configuration dimension (replacing quality_tier), joint_complexity task selection factor, and inter-spec sequencing gates. Key features: 4 paintable sealant types (acrylic_latex, siliconized_acrylic, polyurethane, hybrid_ms), 2 joint complexity tiers (simple_bead, backer_rod), silicone exclusion (never paintable), polyurethane 3-7 day cure scheduling gate (GATE_CAULK_POLY_CURE), backer rod auto-escalation for joints > 3/8 inch, shared access assumption with adjacent painting spec (no access modifier), 11 tasks across 5 modules (all binary — no QT dimension), 4 material systems (keyed by sealant_type), 1 factor modifier (joint_complexity task selection), 2 round configurations, 2 protection zones, 5 consumables, 8 variants (4 sealant types x 2 joint complexities), 3 PaintScope inputs, 1 paintable item (ITM_CAULK_JOINT LF), 2 cross-spec flags (XSPEC_CAULK_COMPLETE, XSPEC_CAULK_POLY_CURE_GATE), 3 gate conditions (silicone hard stop, polyurethane cure gate, wide joint backer rod gate). No quality tier, no substrate_state, no application_method, no sheen. This is a simple non-coating spec — the sealant bead is the deliverable, not a painted surface.
